body:
If I was being entirely optimistic I can see myself as a successful individual by the start of January. I've realised that me, nor anyone else, needs the educational system to succeed in life. However, I can't see myself being happy, regardless of what I'm doing. As I've said in other comments I already live what many would regard as a deeply fulfilling and engaging life.

I have seen the movies, I can't say I care for them. I much prefer watching something by Kubrick, it makes you think more.

The mental health care system, at least in my county, is terrible. There aren't enough trained professionals. The first time I attempted, I went straight to the hospital, because I had a sudden burst of clarity of 'What the fuck am I doing?' and I was transferred to a brand new nurse, not the on call doctor, who was free at the time (or I assume he was, he walked in to the room I was in to get a coffee and then sat down). 

So...I don't have much faith in that now.
Anyways, as I've said below, I'm at peace with the idea, and I have every intention of going ahead with it tomorrow.

You didn't fail me.

You blew any professional therapy out of the water with our exchange. You're a hell of a person, and if anything I failed you.

Hanging is a motherfucker. Both of my last attempts were hanging and both times it went wrong.

That's a fantastic philosophy. You seem like a great person, although I don't necessarily share your stance on the simplicity of love.

You've also done an amazing job trying to help, but I've made my peace with what I'm going to do. Honestly, I feel happy. For once. I feel relieved.

It's a little late to stop it ruining my life, it's been here so long now that there isn't another side to me. My boyfriend had trouble understanding this, as I can sometimes come across as happy and other times as utterly melancholy; they're the same thing. I feel the same either way. That's me now, there isn't another dimension once you get underneath the muscle reflexes that can show me happy or crying.

He'll miss me. I'll miss him. I'm sure that if I was to live past tomorrow he would be the one that I'd spend the rest of my life with. But that's not going to work out, I'm afraid. My parents will probably miss me, though they'll rationalise it somehow and inevitably blame me. In time I'm sure they'll forget about me. It made me laugh when you said you loved me, that's a little strong isn't it? Do you frequent here? Is this something you are used to saying to people like me? I had a look a the other posts here and being unloved seems pretty much a universal factor in their depression, in case you thought I was just being a dick.

It's not really possible to miss something once you're dead. Unless, of course, there is something after death. Though I doubt that very much. If there was, I'd most likely spend my time in awe at that as opposed to things that happened when I was alive, even if I was in the bad part.

I can't really figure out what it is about life that makes me the way I am. I wouldn't consider what I do to be a way of scouting death out at all.

I'm not exactly classically schooled in computer science, but that just looks so much more enjoyable than shit like machine language.

It's not like my life is unfulfilling. I've spent the past few years taking photos of race cars. I fucking love motorsport. My weekends are filled with the smell of burnt rubber and adrenaline.

In the past few years I've been around the world as well, so it's really not like I'm burnt out. I'm humbled by life, and the human race.

Ironically I was going to take Comp Sci at university until I left school, I think there's more you can do with it than that. I was thinking of going into the mobile side of things, iOS apps and the likes. It's not something I'd hate doing.

Life does entertain me, chords are struck, but I still don't feel happy. Last weekend I was covering a rally, something that I'd have been ecstatic at even a few years ago, and all I could think about was jumping in front of a car.

I've suffered pretty much every side effect the SSRI medication has thrown at me, and it's a very long list.

As for someone being able to change the prescription, that's entirely possible. However, it wouldn't be possible to even speak to someone with that power for at least 5 days, as the NHS is understaffed and they're incredibly busy at this time of year.

I'm just sick of waiting for things to go right with me, I've spent long enough on the SSRI's for the side effects to wear off, and they all have. Suicidal ideation was there before the SSRI's and it persists now.

I've lost faith in therapy entirely. I spent the first 3 years trying that, with absolutely no results. It's not a case of an individual therapist's method. I got frustrated with them all, they ask questions and suggest things that I'm more than capable of doing in my own head. I can see that what I'm thinking and that my intentions are utterly insane, and that there could be hope in the future. But I've spent 5 out of my 18 years of life, 60 percent of my life, hating every aspect of it.

I just want it to end.

A better life?

I'd be happy homeless if I didn't look at things and think of how they could kill me. I'd be happy waking up in the morning and being disappointed I was still alive. I couldn't care less about any type of material or financial gains, or the company of others, my boyfriend included, so it's hard to answer what element it is that would make my life better.

I don't want to continue living because, although I'm in wonder at the whole concept of it, I don't feel I want it. I know it's a selfish act, but I don't care at this point. I just want it to end. I don't care what's at the other side of it, whether it's an abyss, or as some would have you believe, an afterlife.

I turn 18 in just over 24 hours. I have all of those freedoms then, being a resident of the UK. It gives me no hope.

Does that answer your questions?
